key: The thirty spokes unite in the one nave; but it is on the empty space (for the axle), that the use of the wheel depends.
s: The chapter says thirty spokes unite in one nave, but the use of the wheel depends on the empty space; Wang Bi, on chapter 11, reads it as saying that the nave can gather the thirty spokes because of its non-being, since its emptiness can receive things, and so it holds the many together.
src: Wang Bi, Laozi zhu, chapter 11, zh.wikisource (the Huating Zhang edition), revision 2354026 (2024)

opened.locator: chapter 11, comment on 三十輻共一轂，當其無，有車之用

evidence.words: 轂所以能統三十輻者，無也，以其無能受物之故，故能以實統眾也。
evidence.gloss: What enables the nave to hold the thirty spokes together is non-being: because its non-being can receive things, it can, with its substance, unite the many.
evidence.licence: public domain text; transcription CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource)

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, ref Tao Te Ching 11, at [10]); Wang Bi comments on exactly this line (三十輻共一轂，當其無，有車之用). His comment says the nave can unite (統) the thirty spokes by non-being (無), because non-being can receive things, and so unites the many (統眾); the sentence carries this, rendering 無能受物 as its emptiness receiving things, which stays within the words. Plain sense faithful and avoids Legge's parenthesis. entry-check ok.
